question: What is the main use of a research checklist in a clinical setting?

options.A: To calculate the exact sample size for a study
options.B: To measure the deep emotional feelings of a patient
options.C: To test the reading literacy of pregnant mothers
options.D: To systematically record observed actions or conditions

explanation: Checklists are observational tools used to tick off specific actions or features as they happen in real time. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T1#BMP225_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why does the quality of a research finding depend heavily on the data collection tool?

options.A: Patients refuse to speak unless the questionnaire is long
options.B: A good tool automatically writes the final research report for you
options.C: Poorly designed tools gather inaccurate data regardless of analysis
options.D: Ethical approval is only granted if the questionnaire is short

explanation: If flawed instruments collect the initial data, no statistical method can rescue the final results. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T1#BMP225_U3_T1_h1)

question: What type of question provides fixed options for the respondent to choose from?
explanation: Closed-ended questions offer pre-determined choices, making them quick to answer and easy to code during analysis. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T1#BMP225_U3_T1_h2)

question: Why must a researcher avoid using leading questions in a midwifery study?

options.A: They are strictly prohibited by international nursing laws
options.B: They take too much time to type out on the questionnaire paper
options.C: They introduce bias by pushing the respondent toward a specific answer
options.D: They cause the computer software to crash during data entry

explanation: Leading questions influence the respondent, resulting in data that does not reflect their true opinion. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T1#BMP225_U3_T1_h2)

question: How should items on a clinical observation checklist generally be arranged?

options.A: Alphabetically by the name of the clinical procedure
options.B: Randomly to keep the observer fully alert
options.C: In the chronological order the actions happen
options.D: By how difficult the task is to perform

explanation: Arranging items step-by-step matches the natural flow of clinical work, making it easy for the observer to tick boxes accurately. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T1#BMP225_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following is an example of a well-written checklist item?

options.A: Communicated effectively with the anxious mother
options.B: Checked the fetal heart rate using a Pinard stethoscope
options.C: Showed great care and compassion toward the labouring woman
options.D: Managed the antenatal clinic session very smoothly

explanation: Good checklist items are specific and observable, unlike subjective phrases that different people might interpret differently. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T1#BMP225_U3_T1_h3)

question: Who is best suited to check if a new midwifery questionnaire covers all necessary points?

options.A: First-year nursing students starting clinical postings
options.B: Experienced midwifery educators and senior clinicians
options.C: Patients waiting in the antenatal clinic hallway
options.D: Computer programmers who will clean the final data

explanation: Experts in the field have the clinical depth required to judge whether all vital aspects of the subject are included. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T1#BMP225_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the main goal of validating a research data collection instrument?

options.A: To prove that the tool accurately measures what it is designed to measure
options.B: To ensure the sample size is large enough for statistical tests
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of printing research papers
options.D: To make the questionnaire look colourful and attractive to respondents

explanation: Validation confirms the scientific credibility of the instrument so other researchers can trust the final results. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T1#BMP225_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is a pilot test when designing a research tool?

options.A: An official government audit of a maternity hospital ward
options.B: The final presentation of research results at a conference
options.C: A small-scale preliminary trial of the data collection tool
options.D: A laboratory test run on blood samples from pregnant women

explanation: A pilot test acts as a dry run to spot errors before investing time and money into the main study. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T1#BMP225_U3_T1_h5)

question: During a pilot test, you notice respondents consistently misunderstand question four. What should you do next?

options.A: Revise or rewrite the question to make it clearer
options.B: Delete the entire research project and change your topic
options.C: Scold the respondents for not reading instructions carefully
options.D: Leave the question as it is and guess the answers later

explanation: Pilot testing is meant to reveal confusing wording so it can be fixed before collecting actual study data. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T1#BMP225_U3_T1_h5)
